engineeringSkip.reason: Beaming structural information via quantum entanglement to rearrange local atoms into a building has no basis in known physics — entanglement cannot transmit usable information or induce remote structural changes.

factCheck.reason: It claims buildings can be materialised at a distance by 'quantum entanglement of material states', but entanglement cannot transmit usable energy or matter, and no known physics lets atoms be rearranged into a structure without physically delivering the material and energy.
